description.summary: private link between the Cacao dock and compositor

protocol.description:
The one private protocol of the Cacao desktop. The window list comes from an existing protocol; this one carries only what no existing protocol does: where minimized windows go, window previews, and the Exposé trigger.
Only the dock is expected to bind it. It is unstable: both ends live in the swift-linux-shell repository and change together.

interface.name: zcacao_dock_manager_v1

description.summary: the dock's requests to the compositor

interface.description: A global the compositor advertises for the dock.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Minimize targets set through this object are removed.

request.name: set_minimize_target

description.summary: where an app's windows minimize to

request.description: Sets the rectangle, in the given surface's coordinates, that windows with this app_id animate to when minimized and from when restored. Usually the app's icon in the dock. Replaces any earlier rectangle for the same app_id.

arg.name: app_id
arg.summary: Wayland app_id the target is for

arg.name: surface
arg.summary: surface the rectangle is relative to

description.summary: forget where an app's windows minimize to

entry.name: all_windows
entry.summary: every window on the current workspace

entry.name: desktop
entry.summary: move windows aside to show the desktop

request.name: show_expose
request.description: Asks the compositor to lay out windows for picking. If Exposé is already showing in the same mode, it ends.

request.name: get_preview

description.summary: ask for a picture of a window

request.description: Creates a preview of one window, named by its ext-foreign-toplevel-list identifier, scaled to fit within the given size.

interface.name: zcacao_dock_preview_v1
interface.description: The compositor first sends buffer with the size and format it will draw. The client then sends copy with a wl_shm buffer of that size, and the compositor answers with ready or failed. After either, the object can only be destroyed.

description.summary: the buffer the client should provide
draw the window into a buffer

event.name: failed
event.description: The window is gone, the buffer did not match, or previews are not supported yet.
